findings.title: Required post check is attached to the base branch, not the PR head
findings.why: The workflow uses `pull_request_target`, which runs in the base-branch context (`GITHUB_SHA` is the base branch commit). The `post` job's check run therefore is not created for the PR head SHA, so making `post` required in branch protection cannot gate the PR as the README claims; it can instead leave PRs waiting for a check that will never match the head commit.

findings.title: Any user can cancel an in-progress review with `/review`
findings.why: The job condition only checks that the comment is on a PR and starts with `/review`; the collaborator check happens inside the action after the job has already entered the concurrency group. Because `cancel-in-progress` is true, a non-collaborator can post `/review` repeatedly to cancel legitimate reviews (and consume runner time with the secret-bearing job).

findings.title: Only the review job is serialized; stale post jobs can race and overwrite newer results
findings.why: Concurrency is job-level on `review`, not on `post` and not workflow-level. Once a review has finished, a later push does not cancel the already-running `post` job. That old post job can post inline comments for the old head and overwrite the summary/walkthrough after the newer run, or two post jobs can both see no summary and create duplicates. The post script never re-checks `result.head_sha` against the current PR head.

findings.title: Gate passes when the blocking count is missing or null
findings.why: `counts.get('blocking')` is falsey for absent, null, or empty values. A malformed or older report with `counts = {'complete': True}` (or `blocking: null`) is treated as having no blockers and goes green, even though there is no evidence of zero 🔴. The gate should fail closed unless `blocking` is explicitly zero.

findings.title: Rejected inline comments are silently dropped if the summary lacks the counts marker
findings.why: When `rpartition('\n<!-- review-agents:counts')` finds no separator, `updated` is just the original `summary`; the rejected comments are never appended. A report summary without that hidden counts line loses exactly the inline comments GitHub rejected, violating D-033's promise that none are lost.

findings.title: GitHub API failures abort before writing the result artifact
findings.why: The `github.ok(...)` calls that fetch the PR and check the head are outside the later `try/except Failure` block. A transient GitHub error raises, the review action exits before `_write` and upload, and the post job then fails at artifact download. In that case the last summary stays up instead of being replaced with a failure, contrary to the stated behavior.

findings.title: HTTPS-only guard does not cover redirects
findings.why: The code checks only the initial URL, but `urllib.request.urlopen` follows redirects by default, including redirects to plain `http`. A 3xx response from the service or GitHub API can therefore forward the Authorization header or request body over plaintext despite the explicit HTTPS-only guarantee.
